note: Defines long chain of thought against short, and names overthinking and inference time scaling as measurable phenomena.
title: Towards Reasoning Era: A Survey of Long Chain-of-Thought for Reasoning Large Language Models

reading.body:
This survey defines long chain-of-thought against short chain-of-thought and names overthinking and inference-time scaling as specific, measurable phenomena rather than vague concepts.

Inference-time scaling, where a model uses more compute at answer time to reason longer rather than more compute at training time to learn more, is a direct compute story, it shifts the cost of a smarter answer from the training run to every single query. Overthinking is the failure mode of that approach, where more reasoning tokens do not produce a better answer and simply cost more.

As a survey, it organizes existing findings rather than measuring overthinking or inference-time cost directly, and it does not say at what point additional reasoning tokens stop helping for a given task.

explain_beginner: Newer AI models like OpenAI's o1 got noticeably better at hard math and coding problems by thinking for much longer before answering than older models did. This survey explains the difference between that kind of long, extended thinking and the older, shorter style of step by step reasoning. Long reasoning has three ingredients according to the authors, going genuinely deeper into a problem instead of stopping at the first plausible path, exploring more than one possible approach before committing to it, and being able to catch and fix its own mistakes along the way. The survey also tackles a live debate in the field, whether models sometimes overthink simple problems and waste effort on them, and it catalogs where research still falls short, especially handling images or other non text input during reasoning, and doing all of this efficiently rather than burning enormous amounts of compute.
explain_business: The operational fact for anyone deploying reasoning enabled AI products is that longer reasoning chains reliably improve accuracy on genuinely hard math and coding tasks, which is why thinking or extended reasoning toggles now exist across commercial AI assistants, but that same extended reasoning consumes meaningfully more compute and latency per query, and this survey documents that the field has not yet solved doing this efficiently at scale. For a business case involving reasoning models, that means budgeting for a real cost versus accuracy tradeoff per query rather than assuming longer reasoning is free, and the overthinking problem the authors describe means naive deployment can waste spend on easy queries that never needed extended reasoning in the first place. This is a live, current tradeoff as of the 2025 model generation the survey covers, and the efficiency gaps the authors flag are exactly the features a business should ask a model vendor about before committing to reasoning mode pricing at scale.
explain_practitioner: Chen and colleagues formalize a taxonomy separating short chain of thought from long chain of thought, arguing long CoT is defined by three measurable properties, deep reasoning, genuine multi step decomposition rather than shallow pattern matching, extensive exploration, search across multiple candidate solution paths rather than committing to the first one, and feasible reflection, the ability to detect and revise an earlier reasoning error mid trace. Using models like OpenAI-o1 and DeepSeek-R1 as reference points, the survey organizes existing work on how these properties emerge during training and reviews the debate around overthinking, where models expend unnecessary reasoning tokens on problems that do not require them, and inference time scaling, where more test time compute reliably improves accuracy up to a point. As a survey, its contribution is organizing existing findings rather than new experiments, and the authors identify gaps rather than closing them, multimodal reasoning integration, computational efficiency at long context lengths, and structured knowledge integration during reasoning itself.
